**Syllabus Overview (based on the provided course materials)**  

- **Thermodynamics & Kinetics (Module 1)**  
  - Introduction to thermodynamic systems, state vs. path functions, intensive/extensive properties [Source: Module 1 Thermodynamics and Kinetics, Slide 1]  
  - First law of thermodynamics, internal energy, enthalpy, heat capacity, and expansion work (isothermal, adiabatic, isobaric, isochoric processes) [Source: Module 1 Thermodynamics and Kinetics, Slide 25]  
  - Second law of thermodynamics, entropy, Carnot cycle, Gibbs‑Helmholtz equation [Source: Module 1 Thermodynamics and Kinetics, Slide 1]  

- **Applied Chemistry for Electronics (BACHY106 – Module 4)**  
  - Semiconductor materials for photovoltaics: silicon types (single‑crystal, poly‑crystalline, amorphous), doping, band‑gap, and efficiency [Source: Module 4 BACHY106 CV, Slide 36]  
  - Photoelectrochemical (PEC) cells and basic operating principles [Source: Module 4 BACHY106 CV, Slide 36]  
  - Electrochemical techniques: voltammetry, cyclic voltammetry, three‑electrode setup, interpretation of current‑potential curves [Source: Module 4 BACHY106 CV, Slide 8]  
  - Dye‑sensitized solar cells (DSSCs): transparent conductive substrates, working electrode (TiO₂), photosensitizer design, electrolyte composition, counter electrode materials [Source: Module 4 BACHY106 CV, Slide 50]  

- **Computational Chemistry (Module 5 – BACHY107)**  
  - Definition and scope of computational chemistry; relationship to AI/ML [Source: Latest Module 5 Lecture PPT.pptx, Slide 1]  
  - Quantum chemical calculations: energy, geometry optimization, frequency, excited‑state, reaction‑path, etc. [Source: Latest Module 5 Lecture PPT.pptx, Slide 9]    - Common methods and basis sets (HF, DFT, MP2, Coupled‑Cluster, CASSCF, basis‑set families) [Source: Latest Module 5 Lecture PPT.pptx, Slide 10]  
  - Software tools and computational resources (Gaussian, ORCA, GROMACS, HPC clusters, etc.) [Source: Latest Module 5 Lecture PPT.pptx, Slide 6]  
  - Applications across chemistry: molecular structure, spectroscopic properties, energy/materials design, catalysis

1. **Focus on the core syllabus topics that appear in the lecture slides**  
   - **Thermodynamics & Kinetics (Module 1)** – Start with the introductory slides that define the subject and the laws that govern energy changes.  
     - *What to review*: the definition of thermodynamics, the Zeroth, First, and Second laws, and the concepts of internal energy, enthalpy, and entropy [Source: Module 1 Thermodynamics and Kinetics, Slide 1].  
   - **Chemical Bonding & Molecular Interactions (Module 1 corrections)** – Make sure you can distinguish intramolecular (ionic, covalent, metallic) from intermolecular (van der Waals, hydrogen, ion‑dipole) forces and explain why they affect melting points, solubility, and material properties [Source: BACHY106 Module 1 corrections, Slide 1].  
   - **Reaction Rates & Rate Laws (Module 1 Thermodynamics and Kinetics, Slide 77)** – Practice writing rate expressions, understanding the role of stoichiometric coefficients, and recognizing that the rate law must be determined experimentally, not from the balanced equation [Source: Module 1 Thermodynamics and Kinetics, Slide 77].
